plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked comparison shows Rumford's Munich cannon box rising from 60°F to 212°F (boiling) in 150 minutes alongside Joule's falling-weight paddle wheel converting 772.692 foot-pounds of mechanical work into 1 BTU of heat (raising 1 lb of water by 1°F = 4.184 J/cal).

teach_overlay.label: 60°F → 212°F (150 MIN) · 772 FT·LBF = 1°F IN 1 LB WATER
teach_overlay.detail: Inked comparison of Rumford's 1798 cannon-boring water temperature curve (0 min: 60°F → 60 min: 107°F → 90 min: 142°F → 120 min: 178°F → 150 min: 212°F boiling) and Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat (772 ft·lbf per 1°F in 1 lb water = 4.184 J/cal)
teach_overlay.scale: 772 foot-pounds of work for a single degree Fahrenheit — you have to drop a twenty-nine-pound weight twenty times from chest height just to warm one pint of water by a single degree
teach_overlay.who_card: Benjamin Thompson, Count Rumford (1753–1814) — American-Bavarian military engineer · James Prescott Joule (1818–1889) — Manchester brewer and physicist
